name: Kiwi Sizing
summary: Shopify size charts and AI fit recommendations, built to cut returns. From Staytuned.
best_for: apparel and accessory stores where sizing drives returns, and that want charts plus an AI fit recommender without building either: 4.7 stars from 1,216 reviews on 19 September 2026 is a strong base, though the recent ones read differently from the aggregate
skip_if: you sell one-size or non-wearable products, where a size chart answers a question nobody asks, or you need more than ten charts and would land on a tier whose order-volume charges are not published
honest_knock: The free plan is not limited by the chart count most people assume. Three charts is generous for a small catalogue; the real limit is the Kiwi watermark sitting on your storefront, and removing it is what the $7.99 buys. Judge the free tier on whether you can live with that watermark in front of customers, not on how many charts you get. And read the small print above Plus and Ultimate before you upgrade: both add order-volume charges that the App Store listing never quantifies, while Premium says in writing that it has none.

pricing.notes: (read 5 September 2026 and re-read 19 September and 4 November 2026 on apps.shopify.com/kiwi-sizing, no amount changed) Four tiers, and the interesting line is not the price but the sentence under it. Free publishes up to three size charts with 22 templates and unlimited CSV import, and puts a Kiwi watermark on your storefront. Premium is $7.99 a month for up to ten charts, removes the watermark, adds Google Analytics and auto-translation into English and Spanish, and states plainly: no additional monthly charges. Plus, the tier the store marks Popular, is $14.99 for up to twenty charts, ten size recommenders and six languages. Ultimate is $26.99 for unlimited charts and recommenders and 22 languages. Both Plus and Ultimate carry the same caveat that Premium does not: additional charges apply based on order volume, and the listing does not say what those charges are. Import credits are an optional add-on on every paid tier, and all three come with a 14-day free trial. The listing adds that all charges are billed in USD and that recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. So the cheapest paid plan is the only one whose bill you can predict, and the one the store pushes is not.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Kiwi Size Chart (Kiwi Sizing) on a Shopify development store: the install, one size chart made from a template and published for 23 products (not seen in the storefront), the locked Size Recommender, the Shopify approval screen for Plus (not approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no theme change was made. Install: the install form in our own tab did nothing when submitted, so a click on Install in the App Store listing was used; it opened the Install app dialog in the same tab with access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was clicked at about 15:52 (Dutch time). The app is called Kiwi Size Chart in the admin (by Staytuned) and Kiwi Size Chart & Recommender in the App Store. It opened at once, without a payment screen and without a plan choice, on the free plan. The dashboard showed Create your first Size Chart, 0 / 3 completed and Credit Balance: 5 (5 free import credits). No vendor account, call, demo or phone number was asked. Core action, a size chart: Add New Size Chart, the template Tops (product), the name Snowboard size chart, Add new matching condition, All products and Save gave the message Changes saved! Please allow a few minutes for the updates to appear on your store. The result was ready at about 15:55, about 3 minutes and 5 steps after the start: Matched with 23 products and the status Published, with the notice You did not select a unit type (turn on automatic unit conversions by adding a unit type). The dashboard then showed Showing 1 size charts, 2 / 3 completed and the block Size Chart on Your Store with the status Disabled and an Enable button, because the theme extension was off. The storefront was not seen: the theme extension was not switched on and the chart was not opened in the theme preview, so the chart on a product page and the watermark of the free plan were not seen. The Size Recommender block was locked (Start Setting Up Size Recommender) with a link Change to Plus Plan. A chat bubble of the vendor kept appearing (partly in Dutch). Plans: the app shows no plan page. The link Change to Plus Plan opened Redirecting to charge page and then the Shopify screen Approve subscription: This app bills you for a recurring subscription and usage charges; You will not be billed for this test charge; the plan Plus Subscription (monthly) at $14,99 USD every 30 days; You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec; subtotal $14,99 plus any applicable taxes, total due 1 Dec $14,99, with a note that the subtotal contains only the subscription fee and that usage is charged on top, which is variable; App spending limit: you will be charged based on how you use this app, to a maximum of $350,00 USD per 30 days. The amount of the usage charges is not on the screen. The screen also had an Add payment method row, so although it carried the test charge sentence we did not approve it; no card was entered. The Shopify plan page of the app (charges, pricing plans) said No plans are available for your store. The App Store listing agrees with Plus at $14.99, the 14-day trial and extra charges by order volume; the cap of $350 per 30 days is not in the listing. Premium and Ultimate were not seen in the app. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Kiwi Size Chart, the menu and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Kiwi Size Chart? says that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled and left the installed list. Not tested: the chart in the storefront and the watermark, the size recommender, the CSV import, the import from an image or a product description, translations, Premium and Ultimate, the chart limit of the free plan and approving a plan. Clean up: the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps; other apps were not touched; no theme change was made; our tabs were closed (an empty new tab outside our tab group may remain). No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The chart was published in the admin but the app said that the extension on the store was disabled, so it was never seen on a product page; the app has no plan page and the Plus plan is reached through a locked block; the Plus approval screen had the test charge sentence and an Add payment method row, and a spending limit of $350,00 per 30 days that the listing does not mention; a chat bubble of the vendor kept appearing; the app has a different name in the admin and in the App Store.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Kiwi Size Chart (Kiwi Sizing) on a Shopify development store: the install, one size chart made from a template and published for 23 products (not seen in the storefront), the locked Size Recommender, the Shopify approval screen for Plus (not approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no theme change was made. Install: the install form in our own tab did nothing when submitted, so a click on Install in the App Store listing was used; it opened the Install app dialog in the same tab with access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was clicked at about 15:52 (Dutch time). The app is called Kiwi Size Chart in the admin (by Staytuned) and Kiwi Size Chart & Recommender in the App Store. It opened at once, without a payment screen and without a plan choice, on the free plan. The dashboard showed Create your first Size Chart, 0 / 3 completed and Credit Balance: 5 (5 free import credits). No vendor account, call, demo or phone number was asked. Core action, a size chart: Add New Size Chart, the template Tops (product), the name Snowboard size chart, Add new matching condition, All products and Save gave the message Changes saved! Please allow a few minutes for the updates to appear on your store. The result was ready at about 15:55, about 3 minutes and 5 steps after the start: Matched with 23 products and the status Published, with the notice You did not select a unit type (turn on automatic unit conversions by adding a unit type). The dashboard then showed Showing 1 size charts, 2 / 3 completed and the block Size Chart on Your Store with the status Disabled and an Enable button, because the theme extension was off. The storefront was not seen: the theme extension was not switched on and the chart was not opened in the theme preview, so the chart on a product page and the watermark of the free plan were not seen. The Size Recommender block was locked (Start Setting Up Size Recommender) with a link Change to Plus Plan. A chat bubble of the vendor kept appearing (partly in Dutch). Plans: the app shows no plan page. The link Change to Plus Plan opened Redirecting to charge page and then the Shopify screen Approve subscription: This app bills you for a recurring subscription and usage charges; You will not be billed for this test charge; the plan Plus Subscription (monthly) at $14,99 USD every 30 days; You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec; subtotal $14,99 plus any applicable taxes, total due 1 Dec $14,99, with a note that the subtotal contains only the subscription fee and that usage is charged on top, which is variable; App spending limit: you will be charged based on how you use this app, to a maximum of $350,00 USD per 30 days. The amount of the usage charges is not on the screen. The screen also had an Add payment method row, so although it carried the test charge sentence we did not approve it; no card was entered. The Shopify plan page of the app (charges, pricing plans) said No plans are available for your store. The App Store listing agrees with Plus at $14.99, the 14-day trial and extra charges by order volume; the cap of $350 per 30 days is not in the listing. Premium and Ultimate were not seen in the app. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Kiwi Size Chart, the menu and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Kiwi Size Chart? says that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled and left the installed list. Not tested: the chart in the storefront and the watermark, the size recommender, the CSV import, the import from an image or a product description, translations, Premium and Ultimate, the chart limit of the free plan and approving a plan. Clean up: the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps; other apps were not touched; no theme change was made; our tabs were closed (an empty new tab outside our tab group may remain). No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The chart was published in the admin but the app said that the extension on the store was disabled, so it was never seen on a product page; the app has no plan page and the Plus plan is reached through a locked block; the Plus approval screen had the test charge sentence and an Add payment method row, and a spending limit of $350,00 per 30 days that the listing does not mention; a chat bubble of the vendor kept appearing; the app has a different name in the admin and in the App Store.
